sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section contains the header and date of the maamar for Shabbos Naso, 14 Sivan 5732.

translations.translation: With the help of Heaven.
Shabbos Parshas Naso,
14 Sivan 5732

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section introduces the verse about Nasanel ben Tzuar offering on the second day and questions why he did not offer first, given his two merits.

translations.translation: "On the second day, Nasanel ben Tzuar, the prince of Yissachar, brought his offering, etc."
And Rashi explains: What is the meaning of "he brought, he brought" twice? Because of two things he merited to bring [the offering] second among the tribes:
One, that they were knowledgeable in Torah, as it is said,
"And of the sons of Yissachar, those who had understanding of the times," and the other, that they gave advice to the princes to volunteer these offerings.
And it needs to be understood,
For according to these two reasons, it would seemingly have been fitting for him to bring [the offering] first among the tribes.
And even more so, it is not understood,
for it is stated in the Midrash,
"Why is 'he brought' stated regarding him? Because he merited through the counsel of the princes, Scripture credits him as if he brought [the offering] first."
Based on this, the reason for this—that in actuality Yehudah brought first and Yissachar brought on the second day—needs to be understood even more.
Also, it needs to be understood regarding the statement "Nasanel ben Tzuar, the prince of Yissachar,"
that it precedes his name
(Nasanel ben Tzuar)
before saying that he was the prince of Yissachar,
for seemingly,
since that he brought his offering is because he was the prince of Yissachar,
it should have said "the prince of Yissachar"
(and afterwards)
"Nasanel ben Tzuar,"
as it is written regarding the other princes who brought offerings after the second day, where first it says "the prince of the children of..." and afterwards the name of the prince is stated.
And likewise, regarding the prince who brought on the first day, it is stated,
"Nachshon ben Aminadav, of the tribe of Yehudah,"
[where] first [comes] "Nachshon ben Aminadav" and afterwards "of the tribe of Yehudah."

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the precedence of Nasanel's name hints that his personal merit, alluded to in his name, was the reason he brought the offering second and was credited as if first.

translations.translation: B)
And it can be explained based on what is stated in the Midrash
on the verse "Nachshon ben Aminadav, of the tribe of Yehudah":
"Why was his name called Nachshon? Because he descended first into the waves of the sea... He who sanctified My name at the sea shall bring [the offering] first."
And it can be said,
that this precision of the Midrash—"Why was his name called Nachshon"
(which it does not precisely ask regarding the other princes)—
is
because from the language of the verse "Nachshon ben Aminadav, of the tribe of Yehudah"
(and not "the prince of Yehudah")
it implies that his being the one who brought the offering on the first day is
(not only because of the virtue of the tribe of Yehudah,
but also)
due to his own personal virtue,
and since a person's name alludes to his essence
(and his virtue),
therefore it precisely asks why his name was called Nachshon.
And it explains that Nachshon's virtue
(alluded to in his name)
is that he sanctified the name
(of the Holy One, blessed be He)
and therefore he brought [the offering] first.
And it can be said similarly regarding "Nasanel ben Tzuar, the prince of Yissachar,"
that the verse precedes "Nasanel ben Tzuar" before "the prince of Yissachar,"
is
to hint
that his bringing [the offering] on the second day
(immediately after Yehudah),
and moreover, that Scripture credits him as if he brought [the offering] first
(before Yehudah),
is because of the virtue within him that is alluded to in his name.
And although it is stated regarding him "the prince of Yissachar"
[unlike Nachshon, regarding whom it is stated "of the tribe of Yehudah"]
from which it is proven that his bringing [the offering] on the second day
[and also that Scripture credits him as if he brought [the offering] first]
is due to the virtue of the tribe of Yissachar,
nevertheless, "Nasanel ben Tzuar" is stated before "the prince of Yissachar,"
because this virtue of the tribe of Yissachar
[for which he brought on the second day and as if he brought first]
is alluded to in the name "Nasanel ben Tzuar."
